Marketing Environment

slides.title: Marketing Environment
slides.text:
Marketing Environment
A company’s marketing environment consists of the actors and forces outside of marketing that affect marketing management ability to build and maintain successful relationships with target customers.

bullets.text: A company’s marketing environment consists of the actors and forces outside of marketing that affect marketing management ability to build and maintain successful relationships with target customers.

slides.text:
Micro environment
It consists of the actors close to the company that directly affects its ability to serve its customers.

bullets.text: Micro environment

slides.title: The Company
slides.text:
The Company
Groups such as top management, finance, research and development (R&D), purchasing, operations, and accounting.
Internal departments have an impact on the marketing department’s plans and actions.
Suppliers
Suppliers form an important link in the company’s overall customer value delivery network.
They provide the resources needed by the company to produce its goods and services.
Supply shortages or delays, labor strikes, and other events.

slides.title: Marketing Intermediaries
slides.text:
Marketing Intermediaries
Firms that help the company to promote, sell, and distribute its goods to final buyers.
Include retailers, logistics firms, marketing services agencies, and financial intermediaries

slides.title: Competitors
slides.text:
Competitors
A company must provide greater customer value and satisfaction than its competitors do.
Public
Any group that has an actual or potential interest in or impact on an organization’s ability to achieve its objectives.
Media, Local Public, Labor Union, consumer organizations, Environmental groups

slides.title: The Demographic Environment
slides.text:
The Demographic Environment
Demography is the study of human populations in terms of size, density, location, age, gender, diversity, race, occupation, and other statistics.

bullets.text: Demography is the study of human populations in terms of size, density, location, age, gender, diversity, race, occupation, and other statistics.

slides.title: The Economic Environment
slides.text:
The Economic Environment
Markets require buying power as well as people. The economic environment consists of economic factors that affect consumer purchasing power and spending patterns.
Example: inflation, interest rates, employment, GDP
Changes in Consumer Spending.

slides.title: The Natural Environment
slides.text:
The Natural Environment
The natural environment involves the natural resources that are needed as inputs by marketers or that are affected by marketing activities.

bullets.text: The natural environment involves the natural resources that are needed as inputs by marketers or that are affected by marketing activities.

slides.text:
The Technological Environment
Forces that create new technologies, creating new product and market opportunities.

The political environment consists of laws, change in government agencies, and

given society.
